title: Review Arbiter Verdict
description: The output payload the review-arbiter returns when ruling on ONE code-review finding: in the external-review pattern (flow-external-review), or on a realism check (flow-implementation §5), where `realism` carries the ruling. This file defines the SHAPE and value domains ONLY; the ruling SEMANTICS (recommended-default rule, ALREADY_RESOLVED-vs-false-positive, the ESCALATE hatch, the three standing duties) live in the review-arbiter agent + the standard-judging constitution. How the orchestrator ROUTES and VALIDATES this payload (the verdict->disposition map, the standing-duty completeness gate, the already_resolved_by->resolved_by_commit field mapping) lives in flow-external-review. `verdict` is the FULL arbiter set (see finding-verdict.schema.json); `severity` is the ONE anchored scale (see severity.schema.json). Return ONLY an object conforming to this schema.

verdict.description: The arbiter's ruling on this finding.

severity.description: The arbiter's evidence-based severity grade for this finding.

evidence.description: The deciding file:line proof — what was verified in the code.

recommended_action.description: The default to apply. Always required — the rule for what it must be lives in the review-arbiter agent + standard-judging.

secondary_actions.description: Additional outcomes beyond the primary verdict, for a genuinely compound ruling. OPTIONAL — omit when there are none.

already_resolved_by.description: The SHA that already fixed the finding. OPTIONAL — present ONLY when verdict == ALREADY_RESOLVED.

option_completeness.description: Standing duty 1: whether the disposition set is complete, or the missing/compound outcome. Full duty definition lives in the review-arbiter agent + standard-judging.

shared_blind_spot.description: Standing duty 2: any agreed position the code actually contradicts. Full duty definition lives in the review-arbiter agent + standard-judging.

confidence.description: Standing duty 3: the arbiter's stated confidence in the ruling. REQUIRED every time.

item.description: OPTIONAL in this shape; REQUIRED on every re-check ruling (re-check mode), where it names the set-aside item ruled on in ONE key format, each the value of the render's item map: `<finding id>` (e.g. SEC-004; review-update-status.sh --id) | `speculative:<key>` (the 12 hex digits of the review render's REVIEW_ITEM_<n>=speculative:<key>; review-update-status.sh --speculative-key) | `handoff:<N>` (the 1-based N of REVIEW_ITEM_<n>=handoff:<N>; review-update-status.sh --handoff-index) | `not_tested:<N>` (the entry's number in the test-plan render's Not tested list, which runs on after the tests and the rejected proposals; test-plan-recheck.sh --not-tested). The verdict is recorded against that item: an escalated re-check takes its reason as --recheck-reason, a survived or cleared one its file:line evidence as --recheck-proof.

realism.description: OPTIONAL. Present only on a realism check — an on-demand ruling on whether one reported item's trigger is realistic: a finding of any severity or class, or a speculative entry (review-core, Realism test; flow-implementation §5).
